bills.title: An Act to Make Small Plug-in Solar Generation Devices Accessible for All Maine Residents to Address the Energy Affordability Crisis
bills.last_action: Signed by the Governor; Public Law, Chapter 644
bills.effective_date_note: Derived: the law has no emergency clause, so it took effect on the general effective date for the session (July 29, 2026), as published by the Maine Legislature.

max_watts_ac.detail: Up to 420 watts AC combined per service address with no electrician. From 420 to 1,200 watts, each system must be installed by a Maine-licensed electrician on a dedicated circuit with a single outlet (35-A MRSA 3475(3)).

rule_sources.title: Public Law 2025, chapter 644 (LD 1730), printed chapter
rule_sources.note: The site labels chaptered text as unofficial until the Session Laws are published.

max_watts_dc.detail: Limits are on export capacity and inverter output.

rule_sources.title: Public Law 2025, chapter 644 (LD 1730), printed chapter
rule_sources.note: The site labels chaptered text as unofficial until the Session Laws are published.

battery_allowed.detail: Plug-in battery systems (AC-coupled storage that plugs into an outlet) are eligible systems within the same limits (3475(1)(A), (1)(C)).

rule_sources.title: Public Law 2025, chapter 644 (LD 1730), printed chapter
rule_sources.note: The site labels chaptered text as unofficial until the Session Laws are published.

utility_notification_required.detail: Only for systems over 420 watts: notify the transmission and distribution utility within 30 days after installation on a PUC form (3475(5)).

rule_sources.title: Public Law 2025, chapter 644 (LD 1730), printed chapter
rule_sources.note: The site labels chaptered text as unofficial until the Session Laws are published.

utility_approval_required.detail: A utility may not require approval, an interconnection application or study, fees, or extra equipment, and may not deny a compliant system (3475(5)-(6)).

rule_sources.title: Public Law 2025, chapter 644 (LD 1730), printed chapter
rule_sources.note: The site labels chaptered text as unofficial until the Session Laws are published.

landlord_provisions.detail: No landlord-consent rule. A customer using a structure they do not own must not compromise it or violate building, fire or zoning codes, and must restore it on removal (3475(8)).

rule_sources.title: Public Law 2025, chapter 644 (LD 1730), printed chapter
rule_sources.note: The site labels chaptered text as unofficial until the Session Laws are published.

hoa_provisions.detail: The law does not mention HOAs or covenants.

rule_sources.title: Public Law 2025, chapter 644 (LD 1730), printed chapter
rule_sources.note: The site labels chaptered text as unofficial until the Session Laws are published.

certification_required.detail: Eligible systems are listed or certified to UL 3700, to a comparable NRTL standard, or configured per the National Electrical Code adopted by the Electricians' Examining Board (3475(1)(A)). Inverters must shut off within 0.2 seconds if power is disrupted.

rule_sources.title: Public Law 2025, chapter 644 (LD 1730), printed chapter
rule_sources.note: The site labels chaptered text as unofficial until the Session Laws are published.

net_metering_excluded.detail: An eligible system may not be used for net energy billing (3475(4)).

rule_sources.title: Public Law 2025, chapter 644 (LD 1730), printed chapter
rule_sources.note: The site labels chaptered text as unofficial until the Session Laws are published.

watch_notes: Watch for the PUC notification form for systems over 420 watts and for how utilities treat the "configured per the National Electrical Code" route.

summary_plain: Vermont's law took effect July 1, 2026. You may plug in devices with a combined inverter capacity of up to 1,200 watts per meter, but only if the device is certified to UL 3700 and your home has a smart meter. Power you send to the grid is not paid for, and net-metering customers cannot also use one.
watch_notes: The UL 3700 requirement means few products qualify today. Check whether a kit's whole system, not just its inverter, carries the certification.
